pages.title: Artemis IV - NASA
pages.description: NASA is targeting the first Artemis lunar landing in early 2028. After launching the crew aboard the Orion spacecraft, they will transfer to a commercial lunar lander for transport to the surface of the Moon. Lander readiness will determine which provider will safely carry them to the surface and back to Orion in lunar orbit before the crew returns home aboard Orion—splashing down safely in the Pacific Ocean.

Остаёться вопрос - где автобусы и такси? Инфраструктура Есть открытый душ, кран для мития ног, небольшая унисекс раздевалка, рестораны. Гостинные везде. Типо проблема - не туристический район. Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year. No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed. The Austrian and Swiss governments have both confirmed the release of their citizens. The Swiss government said Abbt was free and on her way back to Switzerland, while Austria said Gretzmacher had been released after "intensive diplomatic efforts". "We are all very relieved that Eva G. is free again after more than 21 months... Close b-jazz Mapper since: May 07, 2017 Last map edit: November 16, 2026 My Story One of things I like to do when meeting new mappers is ask them how they discovered and started contributing to OSM. Well my story goes back to the very, very early days of OSM. I heard about it through some forums (I don’t even remember which) and took a look at it. To say that the tools were in their infancy would be an understatement. There were no aerial images to make use of, things were mostly done through GPS tracks. Living in the heart of Silicon Valley, there were already some roads mapped out. There were areas right where I lived that were definitely wrong, but the tools just weren’t there for me to invest time, so I walked away for several years. Many years later, I was doing some geocaching in my spare time and there was a big stink when geocaching.com moved from Google maps to OSM. At the time, I didn’t get why they would do that. (A while later it became painfully obvious as I realized that Google was charging through the nose for high traffic users of their services.) I didn’t really pick up OSM at that time either. Written 2025-10-30… Published 2026-11-03 About three years ago, during my day-to-day mapping activities, I came across a golf course that had some obvious errors. I didn’t think much of it at the time. Just a fairway that was drawn right across the top of a green. But the more golf courses I looked at, the more frequently I encountered this error. I soon learned about a golf course simulator video game that was built on OpenStreetMap data and was attracting a large influx of simulator enthusiasts who weren’t seasoned OSM mappers. Along with that came various tools to aid in converting OSM data into these simulators, as well as tutorial videos that made some very bad assumptions about how golf courses should be mapped. These factors set the stage for some very bad mapping practices to spread around the world. My understanding is that attempts were made to correct these bad habits at the source, but the tutorial author wasn’t interested in revising or removing his video. Combine that with YouTube’s bad decision to hide down votes on videos, and you’re left with de facto training material that is widely disliked but that new golf course mappers have no way of knowing is a poor source of truth.
